review_provenance.note: Per docs/CONSTITUTION.md and the repo rules, same-session critique is NOT independent review. A status of PAPER_PROOF_COMPLETE here means 'read line by line and no gap found by this reviewer', which is evidence that reduces external-reviewer load. It is not an independent formal-proof review and does not close issue #216. Only MECHANIZED status is reviewer-independent, because a machine-checked proof does not rest on this reviewer's judgement.

status_vocabulary.MECHANIZED: Machine-checked in the Lean development under formal/. Reviewer-independent.
status_vocabulary.PAPER_PROOF_COMPLETE: Proof read line by line; rigorous and gap-free to this reviewer. Not independent.
status_vocabulary.PAPER_PROOF_INFORMAL: The stated 'proof' argues from construction/definition rather than deriving the claim. Not necessarily wrong - but it is not a proof as written.
status_vocabulary.PAPER_PROOF_GAP: A specific gap was identified. Must be repaired before publication.
status_vocabulary.UNREVIEWED: Not yet read at proof depth in this pass. Explicitly NOT 'checked and fine'.
status_vocabulary.PARTIALLY_MECHANIZED: Some but not all of the claim's content is machine-checked. The unmechanized part is named explicitly in not_mechanized. NOTE: 'content' means part of the claim's own STATEMENT. Machine-checking lemmas that the claim's proof merely uses does NOT qualify - see P1-T-GREEDY-OPTIMALITY, which stays PAPER_PROOF_COMPLETE for exactly this reason.

mechanization_vocabulary._note: The 'mechanization' field describes formalization EFFORT and is independent of 'status', which describes what the claim is entitled to assert. A claim can be PAPER_PROOF_COMPLETE with mechanization PARTIAL: real Lean work exists and is listed in lean_names, but none of it discharges the claim's statement.
mechanization_vocabulary.PARTIAL: Lean work exists for this claim but does not (yet) discharge its statement.
mechanization_vocabulary.CANDIDATE: Identified as mechanizable; no Lean work yet.

claims.name: Closure-system lattice
claims.notes: Standard closure-operator result. Meet is intersection, join is closure of union, proved from extensivity/monotonicity/idempotence. Mechanized mathlib-free: rather than asserting a CompleteLattice instance, each half (closedness, bound, extremality) is proved separately, which is exactly the content the paper's proof establishes. The paper is explicit that the contribution is not the theorem but the discipline of requiring its hypotheses before using lattice language - that framing is correct and preserved.
claims.lean_names: RaklFormal.iInter_closed, iInter_lower, iInter_greatest, cl_iUnion_closed, cl_iUnion_upper, cl_iUnion_least

claims.name: No faithful scalarization of incomparability
claims.notes: Elementary and correct: totality of the reals forces comparability, contradicting an incomparable pair under the biconditional. Mechanizes in a few lines. This is the formal backbone of the no-ORION_SCORE rule enforced elsewhere in the repo (permits_scalar_ranking is pinned false in the external-agent registry).

claims.name: Projection-collision impossibility
claims.notes: Pigeonhole on a deterministic policy over a collapsed projection. Correct and elementary. The paper is careful to scope it to deterministic policies over the projected interface rather than claiming an omitted fact is uninferable in principle - that scoping is what makes it defensible.

claims.name: Unrestricted open-world completeness is not finitely certifiable
claims.notes: Two-worlds indistinguishability argument over a finite transcript. Correct. Mechanizing requires modelling transcript, worlds and decision function explicitly; the payoff is that the hypothesis 'no complete membership oracle' becomes visible as a formal assumption. This theorem is why no ABSOLUTELY_COMPLETE state exists in the code, and it is directly mirrored by absolute_complete being pinned false in schemas/epistemic-saturation.schema.json.

claims.name: Finite-basis saturation
claims.notes: Knaster-Tarski-shaped: inflationary + monotone gives a fixed point at the first non-strict step, and the stabilized state is the least fixed point above K0. Both halves were already mechanized. The cardinality bound is now mechanized too, on a mathlib-free finiteness development (pigeonhole via a hand-rolled Distinct/dropOne, plus a keep/countP partition of the universe). FINDING (precision, not a gap): the counting half needs ONLY inflationarity, not monotonicity - exactly as the paper's own sentence 'Inflationarity gives K_n subset K_{n+1}' implies. Monotonicity is genuinely required for the least-fixed-point half and is used there. iter_index_monotone therefore does not take a monotonicity hypothesis, so the counting bound cannot be silently credited to a hypothesis it does not use. The bound is stated additively (card K0 + n <= |U|) because natural subtraction truncates; the paper's literal |U|-|K0| form is derived as finite_basis_strict_growth_bound_sub.
claims.lean_names: RaklFormal.iter_below_prefixed, RaklFormal.stabilized_is_fixed, RaklFormal.stabilized_is_least, RaklFormal.finite_basis_strict_growth_bound, RaklFormal.finite_basis_strict_growth_bound_sub, RaklFormal.distinct_length_le, RaklFormal.iter_index_monotone, RaklFormal.iter_within_univ, RaklFormal.distinct_witnesses, RaklFormal.finite_basis_bound_is_attained
claims.encoding_hypotheses: Three things the paper gets from typing or from working with genuine finite sets have to be re-supplied as explicit hypotheses under the predicate encoding, and none of them is hidden. (1) 'F : P(U_B) -> P(U_B)' is not a typing fact when subsets are predicates, so 'F maps subsets of U to subsets of U' is the hypothesis hFuniv, and K0 subset U is hK0univ. (2) The finite universe is an explicit enumeration univ : List A with Distinct univ, which is what makes the keep-length the true cardinality rather than a multiset count. (3) STRENGTHENING, stated plainly: 'every strict inclusion adds at least one element' is supplied as a witness FUNCTION w naming the element each step adds, not as a bare existential. Turning an existential into list data requires Classical.choice, which would put 'choice' into the axiom report and destroy the development's central claim. So the constructive content of the paper's sentence is required directly. This is a genuinely stronger hypothesis than the paper's prose and is recorded here rather than glossed. The iterates themselves are never assumed decidable - only K0 is - which is what keeps the development constructive.
claims.lean_names_note: finite_basis_bound_is_attained is the non-vacuity witness: the bound is attained, so it is not an idle inequality. distinct_length_le is the pigeonhole sub-lemma the whole counting argument rests on; it is proved here rather than imported.

claims.name: Derived-view authority non-escalation
claims.notes: FINDING (PRESERVED, original): the paper's proof argues 'by construction it can inherit but cannot mint authority certificates' - this is a restatement of the hypothesis, not a derivation. As written it is a definitional consequence presented as a proposition, which is the kind of thing a formal-methods referee flags. That finding was real and is preserved here as history, not deleted: it is NOT retracted by the later repairs, it is recorded as having been found and then fixed. The manuscript half was subsequently repaired independently (PR #610, 2026-08-14) - see repair_status. What changed on this side is that the formalization now discharges the claim without relying on the circular step: ViewState is the state space, ViewState.source the canonical projection, and Inherits (every certificate the derived view carries is already reachable from the pinned source) the certificate-inheritance relation the repair_action called for. derived_view_non_escalation carries Inherits as an INDUCTIVE INVARIANT across a composition of derivedView operators and concludes both source-invariance and no-certificate-minting; that is a derivation, not a restatement.
claims.repair_action: Formalize 'authority certificates of Z are a subset of those reachable from P' as an explicit relation, then derive non-escalation as a monotonicity property of that relation.
claims.repair_status: REPAIRED ON BOTH SIDES. (1) Formalization: the certificate-inheritance relation requested by repair_action is now the explicit definition Inherits, and derived_view_non_escalation carries it as an INDUCTIVE INVARIANT across a composition of derivedView operators, concluding both source-invariance and no-certificate-minting. That is a derivation, not a restatement. The previously-implicit hypothesis is additionally the explicit OperatorClass field uncertified_preserves, which the type checker forces every instantiation to discharge. (2) Manuscript (2026-08-14, PR #610, landed independently of this work): the circular proof is replaced - the inheritance condition chi(Z) subseteq chi(P) is stated as an explicit premise and named load-bearing, the claim is derived as an instance of Proposition prop:proposal-non-sovereignty, and an added remark records the mechanization including the non-vacuity witness. PDF rebuilt: latexmk rc=0, zero unresolved references.
claims.lean_names_note: derivedView_changes_view is a non-vacuity witness: a derived view genuinely CAN change, so the result is not the degenerate 'nothing happens'. no_uncertified_composition_changes_canon remains listed because the shared principle is what this instance specializes.

claims.name: Proposal non-sovereignty
claims.notes: Read at proof depth. Unlike the derived-view proposition this proof does NOT restate its hypothesis: the codomain restriction is stated in the proposition and the proof performs an actual induction over the composition ('composition therefore remains inside proposal-bearing or transient computational state until an operator with codomain in canonical state is invoked'). Sound as written. Instantiated against V3State (canon / proposals / transient): proposalGen is the operator form, and the codomain obligation is PROVED for that form (proposalGen_preserves_canon) rather than assumed, so no instantiation can quietly skip it.
claims.lean_names_note: proposalGen_changes_proposals is the non-vacuity witness: a proposal generator genuinely moves proposal state while canonical state is fixed.

claims.name: Negative-history monotonicity under append-only archival policy
claims.notes: Finite compositions of append-only (extensive) updates never lose negative history. Load-bearing for saturation: without it a process could become 'saturated' precisely by discarding the refutations that narrow its theory space.

claims.name: Pairwise compatibility does not imply an order-theoretic lattice
claims.notes: Read at proof depth. The proof gives two arguments and both are mechanized. PRECISION NOTE (not a gap): the prose hedge 'a witnessed compatibility relation is generally symmetric' is a modelling remark, not a proof step - 'generally' cannot discharge a universally quantified claim. The mechanization avoids relying on it by proving the two arguments as sharp statements. (1) symmetric_compat_not_antisymmetric: symmetry plus antisymmetry collapses a relation to equality, so a witness relation relating two DISTINCT atoms cannot be the order of a poset. (2) pairwise_witnesses_but_no_join: a concrete five-atom poset, verified to be a genuine partial order, in which every pair carries an upper-bound witness and yet a specific pair has NO least upper bound. That is strictly stronger than the paper's second argument, which only observes that no join element is constructed; the counterexample shows the universal property can fail outright even when no pair is left unwitnessed.
claims.lean_names_note: below_is_partial_order is an anti-vacuity check on the counterexample: it verifies the order really is reflexive, transitive and antisymmetric, so the failure of joins is not an artefact of a malformed order.

claims.name: Three-context parity obstruction
claims.notes: Read at proof depth; correct and elementary. Mechanized in two halves so that neither half can carry the other. The no-global-section half is proved for an ARBITRARY type (transitivity of equality against a disequality), which is more general than the paper's Bool argument and shows the obstruction is not a parity accident. The pairwise-compatibility half is stated in its exact form - the two charts sharing an overlap restrict to the SAME set on it, and that set is the whole of Bool - rather than the weaker and referee-baiting 'each restriction is nonempty'. Together they are precisely the paper's claim: pairwise compatible on every overlap, no global section.

claims.name: Experience-routing non-escalation
claims.notes: Read at proof depth; sound, and it explicitly cites the proposal non-sovereignty assumption rather than re-deriving it. Instantiated against ExperienceState (canon / episodes / routing), with experienceUpdate as the operator form and the codomain obligation proved for that form. Mechanized in the proposition's own 'cannot increase any coordinate of alpha' shape: the authority order is an arbitrary strict relation with irreflexivity passed explicitly, so no order-theoretic structure is smuggled in.
claims.lean_names_note: experienceUpdate_changes_routing is the non-vacuity witness: routing genuinely moves, which is the whole point - search order changes while authority does not.

claims.name: Training-update non-sovereignty
claims.notes: Read at proof depth; sound. Instantiated against TrainState (canon / params / metrics), with trainStep as the operator form and the codomain obligation proved for that form. Mechanized in the 'cannot increase the scientific-authority projection' shape. The non-vacuity witness matters more here than anywhere else in the family: without it the proposition would be equally satisfied by a system in which training does nothing, and the paper's actual claim is the sharper one that training changes BEHAVIOUR while leaving authority fixed.
claims.lean_names_note: trainStep_changes_params is the non-vacuity witness: an optimizer step genuinely moves parameters while canonical state is fixed.

claims.name: Optimality of reservation-first greedy selection
claims.notes: Read at proof depth, hunting specifically for the hidden matroid/exchange assumption these proofs usually conceal. NO GAP FOUND. The exchange step is sound: feasibility gives |S* intersect p| >= r_p, so if some element of the top-r_p set of p is missing from S* then S* must contain an element of p outside that top set, whose utility is <= the missing one; swapping preserves cardinality, preserves every lower bound, and cannot decrease the objective. Assumption (i) disjointness is what makes exchanges in different partitions non-interfering, and it is stated. Stage two is genuinely unconstrained once the reserved sets are fixed - all lower bounds are already met and unit costs make the residual an ordinary top-k - and non-negativity (iii) is what licenses filling every remaining slot. The paper is also explicit about what breaks the theorem (heterogeneous costs, non-additive diversity bonuses, upper quotas, overlapping partitions), which is the right scoping. PRECISION NOTE (not a gap): 'the top r_p candidates' is not well defined under utility ties, and the implementation picks some tie-broken set. The argument survives unchanged, but a faithful formalization must quantify over ANY maximal r_p-subset (every element of p outside it has utility <= every element inside it) rather than over a unique 'the' top set. This is a statement-precision point, not an error.
claims.lean_names: RaklFormal.sum_swap_ge, RaklFormal.top_subset_optimal, RaklFormal.exchange_partner_exists, RaklFormal.sum_le_of_pointwise_dominated, RaklFormal.sumU_congr_mem, RaklFormal.sumU_keep_split, RaklFormal.distinct_subset_exhausts, RaklFormal.subset_or_witness
claims.mechanized_part: Every non-trivial ingredient of BOTH stages is machine-checked. (a) sum_swap_ge - the exchange step: swapping a selected item for an unselected one of at least equal utility never decreases the objective. (b) exchange_partner_exists - the counting step the paper compresses into 'suppose S* contains a reserved-slot candidate j whose utility is lower'. The paper ASSERTS a swap partner is available; here its availability is DERIVED from feasibility (via distinct_subset_exhausts). This was the step most likely to hide an assumption, and it does not. (c) top_subset_optimal - top-k optimality against the tie-safe IsTopSubset predicate: any admissible selection of at most k eligible candidates is worth no more than a maximal k-subset. That is the paper's second stage, and applied per partition it is what the first-stage exchange establishes. Non-negativity (assumption iii) enters exactly once, in sum_le_of_pointwise_dominated.
claims.not_mechanized: The ASSEMBLY: iterating the exchange across the reserved partitions while carrying feasibility, and splitting the objective across the reserved/fill boundary to combine the two stages into the single statement 'reservation-first greedy is optimal'. This is bookkeeping over the three mechanized ingredients rather than further mathematical content, but it is NOT machine-checked and is therefore not claimed.
claims.status_rationale: Deliberately PAPER_PROOF_COMPLETE and NOT PARTIALLY_MECHANIZED. Per status_vocabulary, PARTIALLY_MECHANIZED means some of THE CLAIM'S CONTENT is machine-checked - as for the finite-basis least-fixed-point half, or the non-escalation shared principle, where a proper part of the theorem's own statement was proved. Here no part of the optimality STATEMENT is machine-checked; what is proved is three lemmas that its proof uses. Labelling that PARTIALLY_MECHANIZED would let a reader infer that part of the optimality claim holds by machine check, which is false. The status therefore reports only what is reviewer-independent about this claim - nothing - while mechanized_part records the genuine machine-checked ingredients. Stretching a status label to fit the evidence is the precise failure mode this inventory exists to prevent.
claims.encoding_hypotheses: Utilities are Nat. The paper states u_i >= 0 over the reals. Nat supplies non-negativity (assumption iii) for free, and the argument uses only +, <=, transitivity and add_le_add, so nothing in the proof depends on Nat beyond those - but the statement as mechanized is a SPECIAL CASE and is not claimed to cover real-valued utilities. IsTopSubset makes maximality relative to the eligibility predicate rather than to the whole pool, which is required for the reserved stage: a reserved item may be worth less than an unselected item of another partition, so whole-pool maximality would be false there.
claims.lean_names_note: subset_or_witness keeps the swap-partner argument constructive. The usual 'not a subset, therefore a counterexample exists' step is classical; deciding membership with a hand-rolled memB avoids both Classical.choice and core's List.elem bridge lemmas, which depend on propext.

claims.name: Authority-preservation invariant
claims.notes: Read at proof depth. FINDING (minor, sound-but-thin): the one-line proof 'the codomain of a workspace-only transition excludes canonical authority coordinates, hence the canonical projection onto authority is invariant' is a valid derivation, because the codomain restriction is stated as a hypothesis IN the proposition. This is deliberately NOT escalated to the derived-view circularity finding, where the restriction is asserted inside the proof instead of being hypothesised. It is thin, not circular. Mechanized with the codomain restriction as an explicit argument, and given in the proposition's own 'cannot increase' form against an arbitrary strict order with irreflexivity passed explicitly.
claims.lean_names_note: workspace_transition_changes_access is the non-vacuity witness, and it is load-bearing for this claim in particular: without it the proposition reads as 'nothing happens'. It shows a workspace-only transition genuinely moves the transient component - access changes, authority does not - which is exactly the access/authority separation the section claims.

claims.name: Coactivation does not imply compatibility
claims.notes: Read at proof depth; correct. Mechanized in two halves. coactivation_not_compatibility is the general non-identifiability statement, deliberately given the same shape as projection_collision: a gate whose only inputs are partition tags and priorities cannot carry compatibility information, so for ANY such gate and any pair it coselects there is a compatibility relation making that pair incompatible with the selection unchanged. coactivation_witness is the concrete instance the paper's proof describes in prose - a reservation-first gate at capacity two with one reserved CHALLENGE slot, which computes a selection containing both a claim and the rebuttal that explicitly contradicts it. The selection is COMPUTED by the gate rather than stipulated, so the witness is not a restatement of the conclusion.

claims.name: New substantive knowledge reopens saturation
claims.notes: Read at proof depth; correct. Directly implemented by audit_bounded_epistemic_saturation in src/rakl/epistemic_saturation.py and enforced behaviourally by PFC-SATURATION-REOPENS-ON-GROWTH in src/rakl/paper_framework_consistency.py, so mechanizing it ties paper -> proof -> code. Mechanized with the non-compensatory structure made explicit: Flat requires EVERY coordinate of the progress vector to be zero, and flatness_is_non_compensatory shows one non-zero coordinate destroys flatness however large the others are - ten new paragraphs cannot cancel one counterexample. The 'until' in the proposition is mechanized as BOTH halves, which is what stops the claim being vacuous: growth_reopens_saturation shows a non-flat round makes the newest flat run empty so no positive requirement can hold, and saturation_returns_after_required_flat_rounds shows the gate genuinely reopens rather than being destroyed. Without the second half the first would also be satisfied by a system that can never re-saturate.
claims.lean_names_note: mem_take_append_left and le_length_append are mathlib-free list lemmas proved here rather than imported, so that the development stays dependency-free and the axiom audit stays clean.

claims.name: Freshness-horizon expiry
claims.notes: Read at proof depth; correct, and arithmetically shallow as stated. HONEST SCOPE NOTE: the proposition on its own is close to a definitional consequence of what 'coverage through t-prime' means, so mechanizing only that would add little. The mechanization therefore states the content that actually carries weight, namely that the release gate is non-compensatory ACROSS KINDS of obligation: freshness_expiry shows a certificate that fully discharges its flat-round obligation still fails once the required cutoff moves past the one its route reached, and freshness_not_compensable_by_flat_rounds shows this holds for EVERY flat-round count, so staleness cannot be bought with more flat rounds. freshness_rerun_restores identifies rerunning the route as the only repair. The order on time is an arbitrary relation passed explicitly - no arithmetic or density assumption about timestamps is used.
claims.lean_names_note: freshness_expiry_witness is the non-vacuity witness: a concrete certificate that over-discharges its flat-round obligation is still refused, and the rerun repairs exactly that. It rules out the reading in which the gate is unsatisfiable.

claims.name: Obstruction-blind distillation is unsound for navigation
claims.notes: NEW. Converts the paper's existing three-context parity counterexample from a curiosity about covers into a CONDITION on admissible distillation. Two covers share their pairwise-satisfiability record and differ in global realizability, so no predicate on that record decides it; a navigator consuming an obstruction-blind distillation will admit a support structure whose every step is licensed and which has no global section. This is an identifiability statement, not an argument against distillation - it names exactly which datum must travel alongside the retained cores. Section 02_compatibility_authority already RECOMMENDED explicit obstruction objects; this makes it a requirement and locates the cost of ignoring it in the navigator.
